document.title: Task 2 · Public transport
document.text:
Urban transport budgets are limited, so governments must choose which investments offer the greatest public benefit. I largely agree that public transport should receive priority over new roads, particularly in crowded cities. However, this does not remove the need to maintain existing roads or improve essential connections in rural areas.

A reliable bus or rail network can move large numbers of people while using relatively little road space. This matters because widening a busy road may encourage more residents to drive, gradually reducing the initial improvement in traffic flow. By contrast, frequent services and convenient connections can make it practical to leave a car at home. For example, a worker is more likely to use a bus if it arrives regularly and connects directly with the railway station. Investment must therefore cover service quality as well as vehicles and infrastructure.

Public transport also benefits people who cannot drive or afford a car. Students, older residents and low-income workers depend on affordable ways to reach education, healthcare and employment. A new urban motorway may offer them little direct assistance, whereas a well-planned bus route can widen their opportunities. Nevertheless, governments should not treat every location in the same way. In sparsely populated areas, a damaged road can isolate an entire community, and operating frequent trains would be unrealistic. Road maintenance and targeted improvements remain necessary in these circumstances.

In conclusion, public transport deserves the larger share of investment where congestion and population density make it effective. The aim should be to improve access for the greatest number of people, rather than simply increase the amount of road available to cars. A balanced policy can prioritise public transport while preserving essential road links.
document.prompt:
WRITING TASK 2
Allow about 40 minutes.

Governments should spend more money on public transport than on building new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Support your answer with reasons and relevant examples. Write at least 250 words.
PPB! original practice material.

annotations.quote: Urban transport budgets are limited, so governments must choose which investments offer the greatest public benefit.
annotations.label: Position and scope
annotations.body: “Largely agree” establishes a clear position while leaving room for the rural-road exception developed later. This directly answers the extent question.

annotations.quote: A reliable bus or rail network can move large numbers of people while using relatively little road space.
annotations.label: Developed argument
annotations.body: Explains the mechanism: more road capacity can attract drivers, whereas frequency and connections make buses usable. The worker example makes the policy argument concrete.

annotations.quote: Public transport also benefits people who cannot drive or afford a car.
annotations.label: Counterpoint and response
annotations.body: Access for non-drivers supplies a second reason, then the rural exception prevents an overgeneralised recommendation. Keep the distinction between cities and sparsely populated areas visible.

annotations.quote: In conclusion, public transport deserves the larger share of investment where congestion and population density make it effective.
annotations.label: Synthesis
annotations.body: Returns to the budget priority and applies a consistent criterion: access for the greatest number. The exception matches the introduction.
